problem.text: A $4 \times 4 \times h$ rectangular box contains a sphere of radius $2$ and eight smaller spheres of radius $1$. The smaller spheres are each tangent to three sides of the box, and the larger sphere is tangent to each of the smaller spheres. What is $h$?

steps.title: Where to start: work with the centers
steps.body: Tangent spheres are hard to picture, but their centers are easy: two tangent spheres have centers exactly (sum of radii) apart, and a sphere tangent to a face has its center one radius from that face. Each small sphere touches three faces, so it sits in a corner with its center $1$ away from each of those faces. Look at the four top small spheres first.

your_turn.prompt: The four top centers form a square. How long is its side?
your_turn.answer: $2$. Across the $4$-wide box, each center is $1$ in from its wall, so two neighbouring centers are $4 - 1 - 1 = 2$ apart.

steps.title: Where the big center is
steps.body: The big sphere has radius $2$, the same as half the width, and it touches all eight small spheres, so by symmetry its center $G$ is on the vertical line through the middle of the box, straight below the center of that square. The distance from $G$ to each top center is $2 + 1 = 3$ because the spheres are tangent.

your_turn.prompt: How far is the center of the square from one of its corners?

steps.title: A right triangle gives the vertical gap
steps.body: Join $G$, one top center, and the center of the square. The segment from $G$ up to the square's center is vertical and the square is horizontal, so this triangle has a right angle at the square's center. Its hypotenuse is $3$ and its horizontal leg is $\sqrt{2}$.

your_turn.prompt: Find the vertical leg: how far above $G$ is the plane of the top four centers?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
By the same argument the bottom four centers are $\sqrt{7}$ below $G$. Careful: the box does not end at the centers. The top face is $1$ (one small radius) above the top centers, and the bottom face is $1$ below the bottom centers. So
$$h = 1 + \sqrt{7} + \sqrt{7} + 1 = 2 + 2\sqrt{7}.$$
The answer is **(A)**.

wrong_choices.C: This adds a full diameter $2$ at each end instead of the radius $1$. The top face is only one radius above the top centers.

verification.verifier_notes: Independent reviewer re-derived the answer, checked the text and figure description against the book image, and found no holes.
